runs.evidence: Timed out after adding only the failing regression test. The implementation remained unfixed; npm test still reported Missing expected rejection.
Real one-shot run added a red test, ran it, added the pre-abort guard, reran npm test, and finished with 2/2 tests passing.
Codex JSONL showed a red test, minimal guard, npm test success, and a final file inspection. The process later waited on stdin, so wall time records task completion, not process exit.
Claude Code produced no JSON output and made no file changes before the 144-second environment timeout; excluded from quality comparison.

Real read-only one-shot run was misrouted into the one-search 700-token fast-news policy. Only one of two requested parallel searches executed, then repeated empty 700-token responses until the run was killed after 191 seconds without a final answer.

Real read-only one-shot run completed with four independent web searches executing in the initial parallel batch, followed by targeted fetches and a structured answer. Review exposed overclaiming of source independence, so a strict verified-news evidence contract was added for subsequent runs.

Real TUI run compacted a 116-message session and preserved ORCHID-731 plus 深海蓝, but the compaction provider calls were absent from .moss/llm-usage.jsonl. The UI showed only a generic Working phase for over two minutes and the operation had no active abort controller.

Real TUI run displayed Compacting context, compacted 68 messages, preserved ORCHID-731 and 深海蓝, answered correctly after compaction, and /cost reported both the compaction call and follow-up call. A separate PTY run aborted compaction with Esc in about two seconds, kept the session file hash unchanged, and logged the failed provider call.

During a live robotics-news task, /btw asked only for ALPHA-BTW-42 but the side agent continued the inherited news task first. It took 62.1 seconds, finished almost simultaneously with the main task, and its model calls were absent from /cost because the side agent did not inherit usage logging.

Real TUI run answered only ALPHA-BTW-42 in 0.9 seconds from the inherited snapshot, used no tools, did not write the question into the main session, and recorded the side-call tokens in the workspace usage log.

Real TUI run requested /loop stop at 47 seconds, but the active agent did not receive the abort signal and continued until 92.8 seconds. It completed all three staged phases inside one nominal iteration, the UI still advertised /loop stop after the request, and the saved state counted the iteration as successful despite the abort request.

A fresh real TUI run stopped the first active iteration immediately, displayed a stopping state, saved currentIteration 0 as paused, exited, restarted, and resumed with /loop resume. The resumed fixture completed in 7.1 seconds, npm test passed 1/1, loop-state.json ended completed at iteration 1, and llm-usage.jsonl recorded four agent calls plus loop:judge:1.

The coding prompt contained 'concurrent read coalescing'; the fresh-news router matched the substring 'current' and imposed maxToolCalls=1. Moss repeatedly attempted alternative read tools, then stopped without editing or running the requested red-green test cycle.

After adding English word boundaries to news intent detection, Moss performed the requested red-green cycle and passed 3/3 tests. Review found that it reasoned about the explicit failed-write invariant without adding a test, and the CLI falsely printed a missing-test warning after successful run_tests.

The final Moss run added the stale-read red test, observed old !== new, applied path invalidation only after write success, added a failed-write cache-retention test, preserved concurrent promise coalescing, and passed 4/4 tests without the prior false missing-test warning.

Codex added both required regression tests, observed the stale-read failure, made the same successful-write-only invalidation fix, and passed 4/4 tests. Its JSONL reported 362,914 input tokens, of which 294,144 were cached.
Claude Code print mode produced no code changes or usable task result in the current authenticated environment before the process was stopped after 232 seconds; excluded from quality ranking.

A deterministic MossAgent integration test called generate_structured and returned invalid JSON on every correction turn. The existing runtime resolved successfully instead of rejecting: takePendingStructuredValidation deleted the schema before the first check, bumping the retry count became a no-op, and the generic completion gate silently released the final rejected response.

A real source-built Moss CLI run called generate_structured and emitted five valid stream-json lines. The final success event included a directly parseable structured_output object with only name, age, and skills. Deterministic integration coverage also proves invalid retries fail closed with a non-zero exit code, pending validation is run-scoped and cleaned up, raw output cannot pass through hidden auto-repair, and unsupported schema constraints are rejected.

The headless result formatter unconditionally emitted total_cost_usd: 0 for every success and failure, including unknown gateway models and cached prompts. A contract test for an unpriced model observed 0 instead of an unavailable value.

A real source-built stream-json run returned OK in 1.24 seconds with cumulative provider usage and total_cost_usd: null plus cost_unavailable: true for the unpriced gateway model. Deterministic tests also prove exact registered pricing is calculated and cache-token usage remains unavailable rather than underestimated.

A real source-built one-shot request asked only for OK and forbade tools. It still injected 39,057 characters from 13 unrelated bundled RDK skills because the token 'ok' substring-matched description words such as 'cookbook'. The dynamic prompt reached 39,996 characters and became ineligible for prompt caching.

After replacing substring skill matching with ranked complete-word matching, the same request matched no skills, returned OK, reduced input tokens by 80.3%, reduced dynamic prompt characters from 39,996 to 937, and restored prompt-cache eligibility. Regression tests preserve explicit refactoring and ROS2 skill routing while excluding weak RDK matches.

A deterministic 14-intent routing matrix found casual Chinese 'today' routed to web research, a meeting-summary prompt weak-matched rdk-llm-deployment through English stop words, and generic ONNX deployment ranked the LeRobot policy skill above the general RDK device workflow.

The corrected matrix routes office, short-answer, and casual prompts to no skill; ONNX and generic MIPI work to rdk-device; ROS2 to rdk-ros; and the existing coding/research skills remain intact. Real source-built runs produced an accurate two-item meeting summary with 3,027 input tokens and an accurate RDK X5 Bayes-e ONNX deployment workflow with 7,078 input tokens.
